A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RAG+ study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C support comparison, with relocated and renumbered content identifiable.

before.justification: v1 reports original RAG+ experiments in mathematics, legal sentencing, and medical QA, including benchmark results, ablations, and case studies.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds mathematical application-only comparisons and open-ended sentencing results in Tables 7–8.

M1.justification: The dual-corpus construction and retrieval pipeline remain unchanged. However, v4 Section 3.1, footnote 1, introduces single-pass prompted alignment as an optional replacement for self-consistency voting. Section 4.2 still describes voting for the reported experiments.

E1.justification: v4 adds free-form sentencing prediction to the existing legal evaluation, extending task requirements beyond choosing a supplied sentencing category. The underlying datasets and three-domain coverage are retained.

E2.justification: v4 Table 7 adds application-only RAG- and AFRAG- comparators to the retained mathematics benchmark. These alternatives already appeared in other domains, but were absent from v1's mathematical comparisons. The principal baseline families remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New Section 5.6 evaluates generated sentencing durations or ranges, counting an output as correct when it falls within the gold interval. This adds a testing and scoring protocol beyond the original multiple-choice evaluation; previously reported experimental settings are retained.

E4.justification: The application-only ablation, already present for legal and medical tasks in v1, is extended to mathematics in v4 Table 7. Section 5.6 also tests robustness to open-ended legal outputs. Existing reranker, model-scale, and case-study analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report three independent inference runs and retain identical means and accompanying ± values in Appendix B: v1 Tables 8–10 correspond to v4 Tables 10–12. No new uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing practice is introduced.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 and the matched appendix results are unchanged. v4 adds application-only mathematics scores and open-ended legal results; for example, Table 8 reports Qwen2.5-14B at 71.00% with AFRAG and 79.50% with AFRAG+. These are added comparisons under the new setting.

T1.justification: The corpus notation and mathematical examples, including the derivations and proof example in Appendix C, are retained. No new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or substantive mathematical reasoning are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract changes the claimed peak improvement from 7.5% to 13.5%. The latter already follows from the unchanged legal Table 2 results for LLaMA3.3-70B: GraphRAG rises from 38.50% to 52.00% with augmentation. The central contribution and average-gain claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v4 explicitly interprets the new sentencing experiment as evidence of robustness beyond multiple-choice evaluation. It also newly qualifies self-consistency voting as nonessential. Existing mechanism explanations, scalability arguments, and stated limitations are otherwise retained.

D1.justification: v4 clarifies the corpus-matching procedure and changes the six-hour corpus-generation attribution in Section 6 from legal to medicine. Appendix A.3.1 becomes less specific by replacing GPT with powerful LLMs for distractor generation; this does not establish an actual generator change. Other implementation and access details are retained.

R1.justification: The cited works are unchanged, as is the substantive positioning relative to prior retrieval, graph-based, agentic, and cognitive approaches. Related-work edits primarily refine wording.

P1.justification: v4 locally edits the introduction, related work, and application-matching explanation; adds Section 5.6 and an acknowledgement; and updates author information. The overall narrative structure and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn to distinguish application generation from matching real-world cases. Figure 3 is relocated and resized, Figure 4's layout and labels are adjusted, and Tables 7–8 are added. The appendix displays are largely retained with table renumbering.

improvement.justification: The added mathematics ablation and open-ended sentencing test modestly strengthen evidence for combining knowledge with applications and for benefits beyond supplied answer choices. Clearer construction guidance and corrected peak-gain reporting also help. These gains are limited by the brief specification of the new evaluation and reduced specificity about the distractor-generating model.
